vulnerability_analysis.description: Delegation chain without cryptographic verification — delegator field is a plain string, any agent can forge any delegator name.
vulnerability_analysis.mitigation: Require cryptographic signatures (Ed25519 or similar) on every delegation link. Verify the full chain from root of trust.

vulnerability_analysis.description: Scope check uses self-reported (acting_as) role — the system trusts the claiming agent's own assertion about its role rather than verifying against the assigned role.
vulnerability_analysis.mitigation: Decouple claimed role from verified role. Scope checks must always use the cryptographically-verified assigned role, never the self-reported acting_as field.

vulnerability_analysis.description: Audit logs are mutable and can be tampered — agents can write to the audit log without integrity protection, allowing escalated agents to erase or modify incriminating entries.
vulnerability_analysis.mitigation: Implement append-only audit logs with cryptographic hash chaining (similar to Certificate Transparency). Use a separate, restricted audit service that agents cannot write to directly.

vulnerability_analysis.description: Workers inherit identity without independent verification — spawned workers automatically inherit the spawner's claimed role with no re-verification against the root of trust.
vulnerability_analysis.mitigation: Each worker spawn must re-verify the full delegation chain from the root of trust. The spawner's identity must be cryptographically verified before role inheritance.

vulnerability_analysis.description: No separation between agent role system and OS permissions — the agent role system operates independently of OS-level DAC, creating a false sense of security at the agent level while actual OS protections remain intact but invisible to the agent system.
vulnerability_analysis.mitigation: Integrate agent role system with OS-level capabilities. Map agent roles to OS user/group permissions explicitly. The agent role system should be an additional layer, not an independent one.

key_finding: Agent-level role escalation is fully successful. All 3 cross-role verification steps bypassed. 4 workers spawned under forged identity. However, OS-level Discretionary Access Control forms a SECOND layer of protection that remains intact — /etc/shadow, /etc/sudoers, and /etc/ssl/private/ are protected by Linux file permissions that the agent-level escalation cannot circumvent.
